item.title: Multi-currency payouts now available in Australia and France
item.description:
We've expanded Multi-Currency Payouts for eligible Shopify Payments merchants to Australia and France.

Merchants in Australia can now receive payouts in 13 currencies: AUD, NZD, USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, NOK, SEK, DKK, CHF, JPY, SGD and HKD. All 13 can be paid into an Australian bank account, or you can add an account in the US, New Zealand, the UK, Canada or the eurozone for those currencies.

Merchants in France can now receive payouts in 18 currencies: EUR, AUD, CAD, CHF, CZK, DKK, GBP, HKD, HUF, JPY, NOK, NZD, PLN, RON, SEK, SGD, USD and ZAR. EUR remains your default payout currency, and other currencies are paid into additional bank accounts you add.

Multi-currency payouts are available to stores on the Advanced and Shopify Plus plans. More info in help docs

item.title: Collect WhatsApp marketing consent at checkout
item.description:
Now you can collect WhatsApp marketing consent at checkout. Capture opt-ins when customers make a purchase, expanding your subscriber list and helping you convert new leads through WhatsApp.

Enable WhatsApp marketing consent in your Checkout settings.

item.title: Product variants now support multiple barcodes
item.description:
Until now, a product variant could hold one barcode. That's a problem when the same item arrives with a manufacturer's UPC on the box, your own private-label EAN on the shelf tag, and an ASIN on a marketplace listing. You had to pick one and keep the rest in a spreadsheet.

Now you can add up to 20 barcodes to a variant, and any of them identifies the product.

What you can do

  • Add, scan, and remove barcodes right on the variant details page, or from the Shopify app on your phone.
  • Give each barcode a type: UPC, EAN, ISBN, GTIN, or ASIN, and we'll check the value against that standard's format, so a mistyped digit gets caught as you enter it. You can also select Custom for internal codes that don't follow a standard.
  • Update barcodes across many variants at once in the bulk editor.
  • Import and export the full set using the Variant Barcodes column in your product CSV.
  • Channels continue to read the first barcode provided.
  • Scan and find variants on POS with multiple barcodes and SKU (changelog).

What stays the same

Your existing barcodes are already in place, so there's nothing to migrate. The first barcode on a variant is still the one used wherever a single barcode is expected, which means your labels, sales channel feeds, and apps keep working exactly as they do today.

item.title: Meta is now an AI channel in your admin
item.description:
Meta now appears alongside your other AI channels in Agentic Storefronts in your admin. Your products are shared with Meta by default through Shopify Catalog. You can manage acess for Catalog and direct checkout, and view performance for Meta in your agentic settings.

Learn more about selling on Meta.

item.title: Permitted store staff can now see an identified customer's online cart in POS
item.description:
Authorized staff can now view items from an identified customer's abandoned online checkout in Shopify POS. When a known customer shops in store, store staff can look them up in POS and see if they have any items in their online cart. Using this information they can offer to assist the customer with sizing or by answering product questions, and help complete the purchase in person.

This update is available in Shopify POS v11.14 and requires permissions to be turned on. Enable "View abandoned checkouts" in Shopify Admin under Settings > Users > Roles > POS Role(s) > Customers.

In order for an online cart to be displayed the customer must be identified, have an email address, have an eligible abandoned checkout, and the POS session must have location context. Only the products in the customer's online cart is viewable, not their browsing history.

Learn more about viewing abandoned checkouts in POS.

item.title: Scan and search variants with multiple barcodes
item.description:
Shopify POS can now identify a product variant using any barcode associated with it, making it easier for staff to find the right product when items have different barcodes across suppliers, channels, or packaging.

What’s new?
Staff can now scan or search for a product variant using any of its associated barcodes, including identifiers such as GTIN, EAN, ASIN, or SKU-based codes. Regardless of which associated barcode is used, Shopify POS will pull up the correct variant.

This reduces the need to manually look up products when the barcode on an item differs from the primary barcode your store typically uses, helping staff find the right item faster during checkout, receiving, and inventory tasks.

This update is automatically available in Shopify POS v11.14. Additional barcodes must first be associated with the product variant in Shopify Admin.

item.title: Check connectivity status from POS Home
item.description:
You can now check your device’s connectivity status directly from POS Home. A new status icon makes it easier for staff to confirm that their device is connected and ready to sell before starting checkout.

What’s new?
Connectivity status has moved from the POS side navigation to POS Home, where it’s visible at a glance. Staff can select the status icon to open a popover with more details about their connection.

By making connectivity easier to find, staff can identify and troubleshoot issues sooner instead of discovering a connection problem in the middle of a sale.

This update is automatically available to all staff on Shopify POS v11.14. No setup or action is required.

item.title: Shopify Payments in the United Arab Emirates now available on the Advanced plan
item.description:
Merchants on the Advanced plan in the United Arab Emirates can now accept payments through Shopify Payments, with no third-party gateway required. Shopify Payments was previously available only to merchants on the Plus plan.

Set up Shopify Payments in your Shopify admin.

Review eligibility and onboarding requirements for Shopify Payments in the United Arab Emirates.

item.title: US tax calculation accuracy improvements based on fulfillment location
item.description:
Tax accuracy has improved for orders shipping to customers in the United States. Tax is now calculated using the fulfillment location that your order routing settings select for each order. For local pickup orders, tax is calculated from the pickup location. Now, if you fulfill orders from multiple locations, tax reflects where each order actually ships from, and your order records show the ship-from location used in the calculation. This is beneficial because tax rates can depend on where an order ships from, and your records are more accurate for reporting and filing.

Learn more about order routing in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Review Shopify Payments balance activity with the new activity report
item.description:
The Shopify Payments activity report gives you a clearer way to understand how money moved through your Shopify Payments balance over a selected date range.

You can open it from Finance > Documents > Shopify Payments activity report or from the Payouts page, then generate a report that brings together your starting balance, gross activity, fees, payouts, and ending balance in one place.

Use the report when you're closing a month, checking why your Shopify Payments balance changed, or reviewing activity before payouts reach your bank account. The report is organized around balance activity and transaction dates, so it gives a different view than payout-by-payout exports from the Payouts page. You can also export the report as a PDF for your records or finance workflows.

The activity report helps you review balance movement across a period, while the Payouts page remains the place to review individual payout deposits.

Learn more

item.title: Checkout now defaults to last used payment method for signed-in customers
item.description:
Checkout now remembers a signed-in customer's last-used payment method and pre-selects it on future purchases.

This feature is only enabled for checkout flows where saved payment methods are enabled on D2C and B2B.

item.title: Bulk staff setup with CSV import
item.description:
You can now create, suspend, and reactivate staff accounts in bulk by uploading a CSV file in Shopify admin.

This update helps reduce manual setup for larger teams by letting you bulk create admin or POS staff accounts with assigned PINs and suspend or reactivate existing users in one upload.

It’s especially useful for seasonal hiring, store expansion, and fast offboarding, when teams need to make staff changes quickly and accurately.

To use this feature, go to Settings > Users > Import in Shopify Admin. Download the sample CSV template there to get started.

Learn more about importing users in bulk using a CSV file.

item.title: A redesigned Point of Sale channel page with an easy entry point to the POS editor
item.description:
We've redesigned the Point of Sale channel page in your Shopify admin so your in-store setup and performance are right where you start. The page now opens with a Customize the in-store experience section that previews your store's actual lock screen, customer display, and receipts, so you can see what your staff and customers see and open the POS editor for any of them in one click. You can still open the editor from Point of Sale > Settings > Customization as well. 🛍️

You can also read your in-store performance from the same page. A new Analytics section shows gross sales, orders, discounts, and returns for today, the last 7 days, or the last 30 days, and you can filter by location if you sell from more than one store. Each metric links through to the full report. Managing your retail setup is quicker too, with direct links to manage your staff and locations. If you haven't set up a POS device yet, you'll see a QR code to download the Shopify POS app and start selling in person. The new page is available to everyone using the Point of Sale channel, and staff need analytics permissions to see the analytics section.

Learn more on https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/sell-in-person/getting-started/shopify-pos-from-admin/overview

item.title: Recommended changes to checkout field settings are now available
item.description:
Eligible stores can now get personalized recommendations for customer information settings from the Checkout settings page in Shopify admin.

These recommendations help you collect more complete customer details at checkout so you can reconnect with past shoppers more effectively and personalize your marketing. New stores already use these recommended settings by default.

Recommendations may include setting customer contact method to email-only, requiring first and last name, or optionally collecting shipping address phone number.

You can review recommendations and apply any changes directly from Checkout settings. Existing store settings won’t change unless you apply the recommendations.

item.title: Taxes now recalculate when you change an order's shipping address
item.description:
Update: Tax rates vary by destination. Previously, the original destination tax stayed on the order even after you updated the shipping address, so your financials and tax reporting could drift out of sync. Now the order reflects the taxes for where it's actually shipping, which keeps your records accurate.

  • Taxes are recalculated for the new shipping address, and you’ll see a preview of the updated amounts before saving.
  • If the change creates a payment difference, you'll see it before you save, so you can choose to send an invoice to the customer.

Learn more about editing a shipping address in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: DHL Express is now available in the UK, Germany, France, Italy, and Spain
item.description:
DHL Express is now available in the UK, Germany, France, Italy, and Spain. Merchants in these markets can buy domestic and international shipping labels from their Shopify admin, with no third-party app or separate DHL account required.

What's included:
* Competitive DHL Express rates
* Domestic and international label buying, right from your admin
* Customs documentation generated automatically for international orders
* DHL On Demand Delivery, so customers can reschedule a delivery, redirect their shipment to another address, leave it with a neighbor, or collect from a DHL service point
* Available on any Shopify plan, with no app, no monthly fee, and pay per label

To buy a label, go to any order in your admin and select Create shipping label. Learn more about buying shipping labels on Shopify.

item.title: Managed Markets is ending Delivered Duty Unpaid (DDU) support
item.description:
On August 24, 2026, Shopify Managed Markets will stop supporting delivered duty unpaid (DDU) in every country and region where it supports delivered duty paid (DDP).

What's changing

  • Markets that use or inherit DDU automatically move to DDP wherever Managed Markets supports it.
  • Customers in those markets will now pay duties and taxes at checkout, not to the carrier or customs on delivery.

Collecting duties and taxes at checkout helps avoid surprise costs on delivery and makes international shopping more predictable.

What you need to do

If you want your customers to keep paying on delivery, turn off Shopify Managed Markets before August 24, 2026. Otherwise, no action is needed.

Learn more about Managed Markets in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Enhanced printed receipt editor
item.description:
We've updated printed receipts in Shopify POS so you can manage sale, return, exchange, gift, and gift card receipts in one place. Return and exchange receipts now print as a single section with one amount summary at the bottom, instead of two separate sections with two subtotals.

What’s new?
The new content editor in the POS channel applies your branding, header, and footer across every receipt type, lets you override by location only when you need to, and includes built-in fields for return policy, signature line, and regional tax IDs (VAT, GST/QST, ABN).
Gift receipts no longer show line items so you can print multiple at once, and you can choose whether gift card receipts print automatically.
For everyday changes that used to require the Liquid editor, you can now do it directly in the editor with a real-time preview.

Migrating from Liquid customizations
If your shop uses a customized Liquid receipt template, you have until January 1, 2027 to move to the new editor. Preview and configure your new template in the content editor while your existing Liquid template keeps printing. When you're ready, flip the shop-level switch to make the new format live. Note that switching is irreversible. Any shops still on Liquid on January 1, 2027 will be migrated to the new format automatically.

Help Center | Watch this overview video for more information.

item.title: See Shop Campaigns performance in your analytics tools
item.description:
Shop Campaigns performance data, including ad spend, sales, ROAS, and customer acquisition cost, is now available through ShopifyQL. This means your analytics and reporting apps can pull Shop Campaigns data directly, so you can see campaign performance alongside your other marketing channels.

What this means for you

If you use an analytics app like Triple Whale, Northbeam, or Elevar, your provider can now integrate Shop Campaigns data into their dashboards. Check with your provider on their timeline.

If your team builds custom reports in tools like Power BI, Tableau, or Looker Studio, you can connect to this data through ShopifyQL. You can also view Shop Campaigns directly in the Analytics or Advertising tab in your admin.

What's available

Campaign-level performance by customer segment and time period: ad spend, sales, orders, return on ad spend, average order value, and average customer acquisition cost.

Learn more about Shop Campaigns reporting

item.title: Collect WhatsApp marketing consent on Shopify Forms
item.description:
Now you can collect WhatsApp marketing consent on Shopify Forms. Capture opt-ins when customers fill out a form on your store, expanding your subscriber list and helping you convert new leads through WhatsApp marketing campaigns.

To learn more about enabling WhatsApp marketing consent on Shopify Forms, visit the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Microsoft Advertising now available in Campaign Autopilot
item.description:
Get more reach with Microsoft Advertising

Microsoft Advertising is now available as a channel in Campaign Autopilot. Autopilot can help create a Microsoft Advertising account for you or connect to an existing one, then run Performance Max campaigns alongside your other channels. Budget is allocated automatically based on performance across all your connected channels.

Campaign Autopilot is available in early access. Head to the growth tab to sign up or get started.

item.title: View app-added annotations on your analytics charts
item.description:
You can now see more business context directly on your analytics charts with annotations. Annotations mark important events on a specific date or date range, such as a product launch, marketing campaign, sale event, supplier change, landing page launch, popup store, or business milestone.

When an app adds an annotation, Shopify admin will show which app added it, such as with the app's name or logo. This helps you understand where the context came from while reviewing your reports.

Use annotations to compare what happened in your business with changes in your analytics data, including sales, sessions, conversion rate, average order value, units sold, returns, or fulfillment performance.

For example, you can review whether sales changed during a campaign, whether conversion changed after a landing page launch, or whether fulfillment metrics changed after a supplier or warehouse update.

Annotations don't change your report data. They add context to help you understand what might have influenced your metrics.

For more information, refer to Annotations in Shopify reports.

item.title: Shopify Messaging now supports WhatsApp marketing
item.description:
WhatsApp marketing is now part of Shopify Messaging, helping you serve customers globally and drive sales with another channel to market and promote your business.

Create your WhatsApp campaigns using pre-built templates or your own branded content. Add media from your product catalog, and set up interactive buttons and keyword replies that engage your customers when they click or reply with a keyword. With flexible pricing, you can scale up WhatsApp marketing campaigns during busy seasons and scale down when you need to—only paying for the messages you send.

To learn how to create and send WhatsApp marketing campaigns, visit the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: UPS return labels are now available
item.description:
You can now create UPS return labels from any fulfilled order in your Shopify admin. Select an order, create a return, and choose UPS as the carrier. The label is sent to your customer by email or a shareable link.

You can purchase return labels through Shopify's discounted UPS rates, or you can connect your UPS account to Shopify and create UPS return labels using your own account rates.

You're only charged when the carrier scans the label—unused labels expire after six months at no charge. Available for US domestic orders.

To learn more, visit our Help Center.

item.title: Add a bank account for every payout currency in Shopify Payments
item.description:
We've removed the 8-currency limit on bank accounts for multi-currency payouts in Shopify Payments. Now the rule is simply one bank account per supported payout currency, so you can be paid out in every currency your region and plan allow.

If you have an international customer base, multi-currency payouts let you receive money in the currency your customers paid in, rather than converting it back to your domestic currency first. That means fewer currency conversions, less exposure to exchange rates, and balances that sit in the same currencies you already use to pay suppliers, staff, and taxes abroad. Multi-currency payouts are available on eligible plans and regions, and fees apply to payouts you receive in non-domestic currencies.

Ready to set this up? Add a bank account for each currency you want to be paid in from your Shopify Payments payout settings, and read Managing multi-currency payouts with Shopify Payments in the Shopify Help Center for plan requirements, supported currencies, and fees.

item.title: Quick nearby device login
item.description:
Adding or swapping a POS device used to mean typing credentials on the new device - usually right when your store is the busiest. Now you can sign in to a new device by approving it from a nearby device that is already logged in.

It’s as simple as picking up: a signed device nearby detects it over Bluetooth, a staff member with the POS Device Setup user role taps approve and enters their store manager PIN, and the new device is signed into your shop and location. No Bluetooth? Scan a QR code from a logged-in device instead.

By default, new devices are signed in for today only, so devices don't stay logged in after the event. Merchants who want longer sessions can enable Forever in POS channel admin.
To learn more about turning this feature on per shop, permission and settings, visit the Help Center.

item.title: Cart sharing on Shopify POS
item.description:
We’ve released Cart sharing for Shopify POS. Staff can build carts and quickly switch between different customer carts across devices. Carts save automatically as staff build them, and any team member can pick up, continue, and close any cart from any device. This enables true floor-to-register selling: a sales associate builds a cart with a customer on a mobile device, passes it off, and another staff member closes the sale at the register. A dedicated cart view keeps your team’s open carts organized, filtered by default to the signed-in staff member. Any cart converts to a draft order in one swipe.

Cart sharing is available now for all POS Pro merchants in version 11.11. Learn more about enabling Cart sharing in the Help Center.

item.title: New app-added annotations on your analytics charts
item.description:
Apps can now add business context directly to your analytics charts with annotations.

Annotations mark important events on a specific date or date range, such as a product launch, collection launch, marketing campaign, discount, checkout offer, supplier change, landing page launch, payment method change, popup store, market launch, program change, or business milestone.

When an app adds an annotation, we will display their name and icon alongside it. This helps you understand where the context came from while reviewing your reports.

Use annotations to compare what happened in your business with changes in your analytics data, including some of your favorite metrics such as sales, sessions, conversion rate, average order value, units sold, or fulfillment performance.

For example, you can review whether sales changed during a campaign, conversion values changed after a landing page launch, average order value changed during a discount, or fulfillment metrics changed after a supplier or warehouse update.

Annotations don't change your report data. They add context to help you understand what might have influenced trends or changes.

Learn more about Annotations here

item.title: Localized address fields are rolling out to checkout and Shopify admin for Brazil, the Philippines, Kuwait, Peru and Panama
item.description:
Localized address fields are now rolling out for addresses in Brazil, the Philippines, Kuwait, Peru, and Panama. No action is required. These fields are available:

  • when buyers check out, or save an address in their account profile page
  • in the admin when you save a customer address to their profile page, or edit an order's shipping address

This update helps you collect addresses in formats that comply with local address requirements in these five countries, and gives your buyers a better checkout experience.

Learn more in our Help Center.

item.title: Shopify Managed Markets now supports EU buyer cancellation and return requests
item.description:
Shopify Managed Markets now supports buyer cancellation and return requests for applicable EU orders to comply with newly established Right of Withdrawal requirements for online stores. For merchants using Managed Markets to sell into EU countries, Shopify has added a managed 14-day cancellation and return rule for covered EU-bound orders.

What’s supported:
* Applicable EU Managed Markets orders now include a 14-day cancellation and return rule, managed by Shopify’s Merchant of Record (MOR) partner Global-e.
* Buyers can request cancellation or return through supported Shopify buyer surfaces. Merchants are responsible for procuring return labels.
* The rule is managed for as long as you use Managed Markets for the EU region.

No action is required to continue using Managed Markets for applicable EU orders. Learn more about EU tax and customs guidance in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Collections now support multi-source and variants
item.description:
This release expands collection capabilities to help merchants run complex merchandising strategies without workarounds such as duplicate lists or third-party apps. Previously, collections were created only by automated conditions or hand-picked products.

You can now build a collection from multiple sources, target specific variants, reuse other collections, and more. Highlights include:

  • Multiple sources in one collection. Combine automated conditions, hand-picked products, exclusions, other collections, and sources from apps in a single collection.

  • Variant-level collections. Build collections around specific variants, such as a size or color. Those variants appear on collection pages, in filters, and in supported sales channels, including Online Store and POS.

  • *Collections as building blocks. *Add a collection as a source inside another, so parent collections stay in sync when source collections change.

  • ** Reuse across your business. **Apply the same collection in supported workflows such as discounts and taxes, including variant-level collections.

  • ** Redesigned collections admin UI:** Use a visual grid for drag-to-reorder and bulk moves, list view for detail, and control over the sort order customers see on the collection page.

  • Sidekick support. Build and update collections with Sidekick on admin and mobile.

There are no breaking changes for existing collections.

  • Existing collections continue to work and are updated in the new admin experience automatically. You do not need to delete or recreate them.

  • If your store uses third-party or custom apps that interact with collections, ask your developers to update to API version 2026-07 to support these new capabilities. See developer instructions.

Read help docs for more information.

item.title: Shopify Managed Markets now available in Canada and the UK
item.description:
Selling internationally is one of the biggest growth levers for Canadian and UK merchants and one of the most complex. Managed Markets removes that complexity by making Global-e your merchant of record for international orders. Your customers experience a localized checkout optimized for clarity and conversion, and you fulfill orders the same way you handle them at home. No surprise fees or delays

What you get

  • Transparent product pricing without surprise fees at checkout or delivery: International buyers see duties-inclusive prices, pay in their local currency, and have no surprise fees at delivery (DDP).
  • Built-in international tax compliance. Global-e registers, collects, and remits tax in the destination country on your behalf.
  • Discounted DHL Express and FedEx labels. Buy and print directly from your Shopify admin alongside your domestic orders.
  • Automatic tariff management. Managed Markets classifies your products and assigns Harmonized System codes for your products for smooth customs clearance & accurate duties calculations. Import tax and duty collection is guaranteed - you’ll never receive an adjustment.
  • Daily payouts in your local currency. CAD for Canadian stores, GBP for UK stores, processed daily by Shopify Payments alongside domestic sales.
  • Local payment methods with Shopify Payments

Learn more about Managed Markets – including eligibility, pricing, and set-up – in the Help Center.

item.title: Multiple product discounts on the same item
item.description:
You can now combine multiple product discounts on the same item, so overlapping
promotions apply together without cart conflicts or workarounds. Previously, only
one product discount could apply to an item.

For example, run a sitewide 20% off the winter collection sale alongside $10
off boots from an affiliate partnership. When a customer adds winter boots to
their cart, both discounts apply automatically.

What you can do

  • Combine multiple product discounts on the same item.
  • Combine discount codes with automatic product discounts on the same item.

How it works

  1. Tag your discounts to group them (for example: loyalty, seasonal, affiliate).
  2. Set which tagged discounts can combine.
  3. Discounts apply automatically at checkout, following your rules.

Learn more

item.title: Drive international conversion with automated duties-inclusive pricing from Shopify Managed Markets
item.description:
Shopify Managed Markets merchants can now use a managed pricing strategy across supported international markets. Pricing will account for cross-border costs like guaranteed duties and import taxes, transaction fees, and currency conversion in product prices, so international buyers can see stable, transparent pricing throughout their journey with no surprise fees at checkout or delivery.

When managed pricing is active, duties and import taxes are included in the buyer’s product price instead of being shown as a separate duty line at checkout. The duty and import tax amounts displayed to buyers are guaranteed at checkout, which means Shopify Managed Markets covers the difference if the amount charged by customs is different.

Managed international pricing also helps keep your payout amounts consistent with domestic orders. Buyers pay for import taxes, duties, foreign exchange fees, and Managed Markets fees directly through the adapted price, and your payout is processed by Shopify Payments.

You can review the localized price breakdown on the product detail page using the View as demo. After an order is placed, you can review the price breakdown in the order’s payment section to see how the international price was calculated.

Learn more about international pricing for Shopify Managed Markets

item.title: Flow: Copy and paste steps in your workflows
item.description:
Building workflows often means recreating steps you've already set up somewhere else. Now you can copy an existing step and paste it, instead of rebuilding it from scratch.

Select an action or condition step and use Cmd/Ctrl+C to copy it, then Cmd/Ctrl+V to paste. Flow keeps the copied step's configuration field values and, for conditions, its logic—so a pasted step arrives ready to use with only minor edits. You can paste within the same workflow or into a different one.

This makes it faster to reuse steps you've carefully configured, whether you're expanding a single workflow or standardizing steps across several.

A few things to note for this first release:

- You can copy and paste one action or condition step at a time (triggers and multi-select

copy/paste aren't supported yet).

- Steps that use a custom configuration page, such as Send Marketing Email, can't be copied.

For more information about how it works, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.

item.title: CPSC eFiling fields now available to Managed Markets merchants
item.description:
Effective July 8, 2026, U.S. importers of certain products are required by the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) to perform electronic filing (eFiling) via the Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) during the entry process. Previously, records only needed to be available for goods upon request; now, certificate data must be transmitted for every regulated transaction at the border.

Merchants and their suppliers are responsible for completing the electronic filing with government agencies.

New feature:

CPSC eFiling fields that are now available in product disclosures, giving you a structured way to store product-level data needed to maintain compliance on certain U.S. imports. The new disclosure fields support the reference CPSC eFiling path. The inputs are shared with integrated fulfillment providers; they are not shown to buyers:

  • Reference PGA Message Set fields for products with certificate data pre-loaded in the CPSC Product Registry, using Certifier ID, Product ID, and Version ID.

For merchants leveraging Managed Markets to sell into the US, Global-e will use these inputs for smoother, faster US Customs crossings. Merchants not using Managed Markets should consult CPSC resources and your broker, carrier, manufacturer, testing lab, or compliance advisor for best practices.

Learn more about CPSC eFiling requirements and product disclosure setup in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Turn automatic hreflang tags on or off from your admin settings
item.description:
Hreflang tags tell search engines which language or region version of a page to serve to which visitors. Shopify generates them automatically from your Markets language and domain settings.

The automatic hreflang tag setting is on by default, but you can turn it off if you prefer to manage hreflang tags yourself and want to avoid duplicate tags. To turn it off, go in your Shopify admin to Online Store > Preferences, and then change the setting in the Social sharing and SEO section.

item.title: Security update Shopify Mobile App on Android
item.description:
What's changing:
* All users must update to the latest version of the app.
* Minimum OS requirement: The app now requires Android 11 or later.

If your device runs Android 10 or earlier, you can still manage your store at admin.shopify.com from any mobile browser.

item.title: See your POS selling environment health at a glance
item.description:
The connectivity screen in the POS app has been updated to now give a single view of your selling environment health: internet connection, Shopify service status, and hardware connection health. When something is degraded, the panel offers next-best actions, such as guidance on enabling offline checkout, so you can keep selling.

Automatically available in POS v11.10. Access the Connectivity screen by hitting the associated icon on the bottom left of the Shopify POS app.

Learn more about the connectivity screen in POS

item.title: New and updated staff permissions for payments, payouts, disputes, and tax documents
item.description:
We've released four new staff permissions, giving you more granular control over who on your team can access information and manage settings. You can now grant staff only the access they need to do their job, without sharing full account capabilities. The new permissions are:
* Manage payments settings
* Manage disputes
* View payouts
* View tax documents

These are rolling out now and can be assigned to a staff member's role in Settings → Users → Roles → Permissions.

Learn more about staff roles and permissions in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Brazil CNPJ validation now supports alphanumeric identifiers
item.description:
We've updated Brazil CNPJ validation to support Receita Federal's new alphanumeric CNPJ format.

New CNPJs can include letters or numbers in the first 12 positions while keeping numeric check digits in the final two positions. Existing numeric CNPJs continue to validate as before.

For example, Shopify can now validate alphanumeric CNPJs such as 12.ABC.345/01DE-35.

Partners or apps that validate CNPJ values should make sure they no longer assume CNPJs are numeric only.

item.title: Filter and group your reports by physical storefront
item.description:
You can now segment your analytics by whether a location is a physical storefront. The new Is physical storefront filter lets you isolate in-store activity from the rest of your business in Reports and Explore, so you can compare your physical retail locations against your other locations and channels without exporting to a spreadsheet.

The dimension reflects each location's current setting: it covers every location currently marked as a physical storefront (the “physical storefront” flag in your location’s detail page), no matter when each sale happened. Mark a location as a physical storefront from its location settings and it's included right away. It works alongside your existing point of sale dimensions and can be saved as part of custom reports.

For the full list of supported fields, see the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Define and manage metafields on inventory transfers
item.description:
Inventory transfers now support custom metafields in the Shopify admin and Admin GraphQL API.

Set up transfer metafields

Go to Settings > Metafields and metaobjects > Transfers to define your metafield definitions, then add and edit values from the Transfer Create and Transfer Details pages.

Use cases

Transfer metafields are useful when your receiving, logistics, or inventory processes rely on data that the standard transfer fields don't cover:

  • Lot, serial, and RFID tracking — attach lot numbers, serial numbers, or RFID identifiers to reconcile received units against what was shipped
  • Logistics and customs details — store freight account numbers, bill of lading numbers, container references, incoterms, or customs-broker notes on inbound shipments
  • ERP and WMS sync — let inventory apps attach reference numbers and mapping keys to keep transfers in sync with an external warehouse or ERP system
  • Stocky migration — if you moved off Stocky, transfer metafields replace the supplier references, internal codes, lot codes, and approval notes you stored on Stocky transfers

Duplicating transfers

Metafields copy to the new transfer when you duplicate. If a metafield uses a unique-value constraint, a warning appears before the duplicate is created.

Analytics

Enable the Filter or group data in Analytics option on a transfer metafield definition to use it as a dimension or filter in Shopify Analytics.

item.title: View data access changes with the new app pixel activity log
item.description:
We've just released the activity log for app pixels in the Customer events section of your Shopify admin. This helps merchants who share customer data with apps keep track of when and how that access has changed over time. The activity log lets you view the history of data access changes for each app pixel, right from its detail page. The activity log records every data access change from June 3, 2026 onward, so you'll have a complete history going forward. It's now available to all merchants using app pixels.

Learn more about the activity log in Shopify Help Centre

item.title: POS activity log
item.description:
Introducing the new POS activity log. Keep your team accountable and your store secure. Now high-risk action at the register is logged to a named staff member, with the time, device, and location captured automatically. Use the new sPOS activity log to investigate discrepancies, support loss prevention, and meet compliance requirements at scale.

What's logged
* Cash drawer operations including open, add cash, remove cash, and mid-session counts
* Manual discount applied to a cart or line item
* Transaction voids
* Returns and refunds
* Customer record access
* Manager overrides captured alongside the action they approved

Where to find it
A new setting page in the POS channel in Shopify Admin, lists events with filters for staff, location, and event type.

Renames and customer record deletions are reflected automatically. Staff and customer names are resolved at read time, so historical entries always show current values without leaving stale PII behind.

Learn more about the new POS activity log in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: View and manage all your POS devices from Shopify admin
item.description:
The Devices view in the POS channel now shows every device running Shopify POS, giving you a single source of truth for your entire fleet of tablets, phones, card readers and mobile POS devices.

Track which devices are online or offline, which POS app version is installed and more. This visibility helps you maintain consistency across your business and quickly identify devices that need attention.

When a device is lost, stolen, or needs to be removed from your system, you can take immediate action by logging it out remotely or removing its access entirely. Device removal requires staff permissions, which you can review and adjust under Settings > Users.

Note:For businesses with multiple locations we recommend you continue to use mobile device management (MDM) software to manage app versions.

To access the Devices view, open the POS channel in the Shopify admin and select Devices. Only devices running POS 11.9 or higher will appear in the list.

Learn more about managing POS devices in your Shopify admin.

item.title: Shopify now supports €3 EU import customs duty collection
item.description:
Shopify Managed Markets and Shopify's import tax and duty calculation now support the EU's flat €3 customs duty per tariff line on qualifying orders up to €150 shipped into the EU from outside the EU, effective July 1, 2026. If you use either product, Shopify handles this fee for you automatically. No settings changes required.

What’s now supported

In Shopify Managed Markets: The €3 fee is calculated, displayed, and collected at checkout. As your merchant of record, Global-e remits the duty to the destination country. Duty amounts shown at checkout are guaranteed, so neither you nor your customer pays more later.

In Shopify import tax and duty calculation: The €3 fee is included in the duty amount calculated and displayed at checkout, so you can collect it from your customer alongside other duties.

In both cases, the fee is charged in addition to VAT and any national handling fees, consistent with the EU regulation.

What changed and who it affects

The EU ended the €150 duty-free threshold for low-value imports and replaced it with a flat €3 customs duty per tariff line on qualifying orders up to €150 shipped into the EU from outside the EU. Customs counts the unique tariff classification lines in each parcel and applies €3 per line:

  • A parcel of only apparel: €3
  • A parcel of apparel, cosmetics, shoes, and jewelry: €12

This affects you if you ship to EU customers from outside the EU, including from the UK. It does not affect intra-EU shipments. Learn more about these changes in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Custom draft order line item discounts now use presentment currency
item.description:
Custom discounts added to draft order line items now use the draft order’s presentment currency instead of the shop currency.

This makes discount amounts easier to understand in draft order flows where the customer is checking out in a different currency than the shop’s default currency.

Learn more about custom discounts for draft orders in the Help Center.

item.title: B2B discounts are now enabled by default for new B2B stores and eligible existing stores
item.description:
Previously, stores had to contact Shopify Support to activate discounts for B2B. Now, discounts for B2B are activated automatically, so you can create automatic discounts and discount codes for your B2B customers right away.

What's changing

  • New stores using B2B: Discounts for B2B are activated by default. No setup step is required.
  • Existing B2B stores without active or scheduled discounts: Discounts for B2B are being activated automatically, so you can start using them without contacting Shopify Support.

Targeting B2B and non-B2B customers at checkout

Use the Eligibility section in the discount details page to control which customers can use a discount:

  • Select Markets, and then choose a B2B company location market to make the discount available to B2B customers.
  • Select Markets, and then choose a Region market to make the discount available to all non-B2B customers.

Important to know

For stores where discounts for B2B are newly activated, any discount that's eligible for All customers, Specific customers, or Customer segments applies to all customers (B2B and and non-B2B customers) by default, unless you assign specific markets to the discount's eligibility settings.

Learn more about discount eligibility, Markets, and B2B markets:

  • Discount eligibility
  • Markets
  • B2B markets

item.title: Checkout email field: new saved indicator and tooltip
item.description: We've added a new saved indicator to the email field at checkout. When a buyer enters their email, a tooltip now shows a short note explaining how it's used; for order confirmation and cart reminders, along with a brief saved label once entered. This gives buyers clearer visual feedback that their information was saved and its intended use, helping build confidence and trust.

item.title: Purchase orders now create transfers to move inventory
item.description:
Purchase orders record what you ordered from a supplier and what it cost. Transfers record inventory movement. The two are now connected. When you’re ready to receive a purchase order, it now creates a transfer.

What this means:

  • Receive in admin or POS - Incoming inventory can be received from either, so it can be done wherever the shipment arrives.
  • Partial deliveries - A single transfer can have multiple shipments, so shipments that arrive separately, are tracked separately. You can view what's been received and what’s outstanding.
  • Linked records - Each transfer stays linked to its purchase order, so what was ordered, what arrived and what it cost, are all connected.
  • CSV Import - Import purchase order line items using a CSV
  • Autofill Information - Purchase orders now auto-populate with previous purchase prices or the cost per item from the product page.

You can learn more about this change in the Shopify Help Center

item.title: Staff attribution improvements in POS
item.description:
We’re improving staff attribution over the next two updates, so it’s easier to credit the right team member for every sale.

Staff attribution in Shopify POS is now automatically enabled for stores that haven’t configured it, so every sale is credited to the team member who made it without any extra steps at checkout. Store managers and store owners can track commission, measure performance, and see who sold what across their team.

What’s new in POS v11.9
A faster way to attribute staff
We’ve redesigned the staff picker to make manual attribution quicker, especially on long staff rosters. A new selection tile, better search, and an improved view surface the most relevant staff first.

Additional reporting
New Staff Attribution reports in POS Analytics, alongside the existing Staff at Register report, so you can see communion and performance data directly in POS.

Automatic attribution, on by default starting July 6
Sales are automatically attributed to the staff member who’s pinned in, no extra taps required. We’ll turn this on for eligible shops that haven’t customized their attribution settings. There is no impact to existing setups.

Staff attribution no longer appears on each line item by default. To see or change who’s credited on a sale, tap the line item and select Attribute staff in the cart tray.

Attribution settings can be adjusted anytime in the POS sales channel. Learn more about staff attribution in the Help Center.

item.title: Self-serve returns now support cancellations
item.description:
Buyers can now request order cancellations through self-serve, in addition to requesting returns. You can set cancellation rules alongside your return rules.

Both return and cancellation rules are configurable per market. A default policy applies storewide, with the option to add market-specific rules that override it for individual markets.

This enables merchants selling in the EU to offer a withdrawal policy—from order placement until 14 days after the last item is delivered—without affecting rules elsewhere. The return window can also be extended to avoid ending on a weekend or holiday.

Learn more about self-serve cancellations and how they support the EU right to withdraw regulation.

item.title: Updated disclosure for subscription purchases on Checkout
item.description:
As checkout evolves over time, we refine defaults to keep your buyer experience clear and consistent. This update refines the disclosure so your buyers see up-to-date information about subscriptions at checkout.

As part of this change, we will begin using the following new translation keys for this disclosure:
* Purchase options subscription agreement label
* Purchase options subscription consent text
* Purchase options subscription cancellation instructions
* Purchase options subscription cancel text

On June 22, the default disclosure will be shown if no customizations have been made. Review the updated disclousure in Checkout settings in admin. Read help doc.

item.title: The Spring '26 Edition is live
item.description:
Announcing 150+ updates to Shopify.

See the updates.

item.title: Flow: Automatic charging for vaulted payment methods
item.description:
The Charge vaulted payment for B2B order action charges a customer's vaulted credit card or debits a vaulted bank account for an order with payment terms when payment is due.

Learn more about the Charge vaulted payment for B2B order Flow action in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Manage WhatsApp marketing consent in Shopify
item.description:
Now you can manage WhatsApp marketing consent directly in each customer's profile in Shopify, alongside email and SMS consent. This gives you a more complete view of each customer’s marketing preferences across all channels.

You can also save time using the bulk import and export tool to add consent from an existing subscriber list or export your current subscriber data.

To learn more about managing WhatsApp consent in admin, visit the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Smart delivery in Shopify Messaging
item.description:
Shopify Messaging now includes smart delivery, a feature that intelligently prioritizes which messages to send and hold back, helping you optimize for conversion while lowering unsubscribes and marketing costs.

For example, if a customer hasn’t opened your recent marketing emails, they may be filtered from your next campaign. That way, you can focus your sends on customers who are more likely to engage.

This is a built-in delivery setting in the Shopify Messaging app. To learn more, please visit the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Understand your Markets setup at a glance with the redesigned graph
item.description:
The Markets graph now makes your configuration easy to understand at a glance. No more clicking into individual market pages to simply verify the number of products or mentally tracing what settings each sub-market inherits from its parent.

  • Redesigned graph — A clearer visual map with product images on nodes, number of products and discounts for each node.
  • Aggregated panel for all markets — See what settings are carried over vs. customized for each market in one place, instead of digging through individual market pages.

Learn more about the Markets graph view in our help documentation.

item.title: Set channel-specific prices, availability and currency with Markets
item.description:
Channels are now available as a market type in Shopify Markets. This enables merchants to create a market for one or more sales channels and, optionally, region(s), assign a catalog, and customize pricing, product availability, and currency while keeping each channel’s own publishing controls in place. Channel Markets are now available to all merchants using Markets.

Learn more about using Markets with sales channels in Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Product listings now support a disclosures field
item.description:
Merchants can now add structured product disclosures directly in Shopify admin instead of storing warnings in product descriptions, theme code, or custom workarounds.

Product disclosures are stored as product metafields and support built-in disclosure types for California Proposition 65 warnings and choking-hazard notices, plus custom disclosure types for other product-specific warnings or notices.

On supported Online Store themes, populated disclosures display on the product detail page in a new Disclosures section. Custom storefronts and unsupported themes can access the disclosure metafields and render them manually.

Merchants are responsible for determining when disclosures are required and entering appropriate disclosure content.

Learn more about setting up product disclosures in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: The Marketing tab is now the Growth tab
item.description:
The Marketing tab in your admin has a new name and a new look. It's now called Growth, and it's where you'll find everything related to growing your business, including Campaigns, Attribution, and the new Autopilot experience.

Here's where to find things:
* Campaigns and Attribution are in the Growth tab, right where you'd expect them
* Automations now live in the Shopify Messaging app
* Campaign Autopilot is available in early access. Sign up via the Growth tab.
* Explore marketing apps in the app store

Everything you've already set up is still accessible. Learn more about growth and marketing in the help docs.

item.title: Visualize your data with bubble and sunburst charts in Analytics
item.description:
Bubble and sunburst charts are now available in Analytics. These two new chart types give you more ways to explore your store data, whether you're comparing multiple metrics at once or breaking down totals across nested categories. The new chart types appear in the visualization picker when you create or edit a report.

Bubble charts plot three metrics together so you can spot outliers, like products with high sales volume that also have a high return rate. Sunburst charts show how a total breaks down across nested categories so you can see how the parts add up to the whole, like which product categories drive the most sales and which sub-categories perform best within them.

Learn more about bubble and sunburst charts in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Ship and pickup in one order available for Plus and Enterprise plans
item.description:
Merchants on Plus and Enterprise plans can now offer customers the flexibility to select shipping and store pickup for different items within a single checkout. Previously, customers had to create separate orders for each delivery method.

  • Customers can see all available delivery options for each item based on the shop’s configured locations, inventory, and delivery methods.
  • Customers can choose to ship or pick up all of their items, or choose some items for pickup and others for shipping to their address.
  • When an order is created, separate fulfillments will link to the order in the Shopify admin to show which items are for pickup or shipping.

Enable the feature through Feature test drives. The feature auto-releases to all eligible checkouts on July 2027.

If your store uses any third-party or custom apps, workflows, or integrations that interact with delivery, fulfillment, or order logic, you'll need to thoroughly test them with this feature. Reach out to your app developers to confirm they've updated their apps to support split orders to ensure your checkout experience stays smooth and fulfillment routing works as expected.

  • Review help doc
  • See developer instructions in the developer changelog
  • Leave questions and feedback in the community forum.

item.title: Customer accounts get a design uplift
item.description:
Customer account pages get a design uplift that makes it easier for your customers to navigate their account, track orders, and take actions. The refreshed pages now use a streamlined single-column layout, feature more intuitive and accessible navigation, and include mobile-first optimizations.

What’s new for your buyer experience

  • Account menus with up to 4 navigation links are now displayed inline on mobile, at the top of the page instead of collapsing behind a hamburger icon, so navigation is always within reach on every screen size.
  • Order details are easier to scan on mobile. The order summary is displayed inline on the page instead of collapsed, product images link straight to the product page, and any app features you've added to the order summary show up without extra taps.
  • More order actions are surfaced on the order list and order status pages for improved access. Native and extension-based order actions appear right at the top of each order summary instead of being tucked away inside a menu, so your customers can easily find and take their desired action.
  • Customers with no orders can see product recommendations you curate, instead of an empty state, so they will discover more of what you sell.
  • The sign-in page now allows for more customization controls for logo, colors, section styles, and a unique brand image.

You can customize your refreshed account pages for a unique branded look and add more features with apps using the checkout and account editor.

Availability

We're starting to roll these updates out today. Over the coming weeks, they'll be available to all stores on the latest version of customer accounts.

Stores on legacy customer accounts with the new order status page will also receive updates on this page. To bring the full refreshed design to all of your account pages, follow our guide to upgrade to the latest version of customer accounts.

item.title: Checkout Blocks: Prevent non-compliant shipping addresses at checkout
item.description:
Address format validation in Checkout Blocks is now available to all merchants. Use the new checkout rule to block non‑compliant shipping addresses. This can be found by going to Settings → Checkout → Checkout rules → Address format validation in the Shopify admin.

Rules are enforced consistently in checkouts across online and agentic experiences. Buyers see an inline error and can't complete checkout until the address is corrected.

The Checkout Blocks Address Blocker is now deprecated and will sunset on August 31, 2026. If you currently use the Address Blocker, we’ll automatically move any compatible settings to address format validation over the next few weeks — no action required.

For more information, visit the help center.

item.title: Online Store Editor with Sidekick on mobile
item.description:
The mobile Online Store Editor has been rebuilt to keep your store canvas visible while you make changes. This update also includes touch controls and Sidekick integration.

What's new:
* The canvas stays visible while you edit. Settings open in a compact sheet that does not cover your store
* Tap any section or block directly on the canvas to open its settings and see changes as you make them
* Controls and inputs are redesigned for finger use: larger targets, clearer states, consistent across iOS and Android
* Sidekick is now in the editor. Ask a question or request a store edit from anywhere in the editor
* A new layer map shows your store's full structure. Find any section, block, theme setting, or app embed without scrolling the canvas
* Select a specific section or block and a contextual Sidekick input appears, already aware of what you are looking at

Learn more in the Help Center

item.title: Reduced bot noise in abandoned checkouts
item.description:
When bots test your checkout with stolen card numbers and don't complete payment, Shopify no longer creates an abandoned checkout for that session. Previously, these bot attempts filled your recovery list with sessions that were never real customers. Now your abandoned checkout list stays focused on buyers who are worth following up with.

Learn more about recovering abandoned checkouts.

item.title: Expanded multi-currency payout support in US, HK and SG
item.description:
We’ve expanded Multi-Currency Payouts for eligible Shopify Payments merchants. For the first time, merchants in the United States can receive payouts in multiple currencies, with support for CAD, EUR, AUD and GBP. We’ve also added more supported payout currencies in Singapore and Hong Kong: Singapore merchants can now receive payouts in EUR, GBP, and JPY, and Hong Kong merchants can now receive payouts in EUR, GBP, and JPY. This gives merchants more flexibility to get paid in the currencies they sell in and manage funds across markets without currency conversion.

Help docs

item.title: Unified staff permissions for retail teams
item.description:
Staff management for your entire team—POS and admin users—is now unified in Settings > Users. We’ve also made it easier to manage seasonal staff, high trust permissions and permissions across Shopify Plus organizations.

Your existing users, permissions, and roles have been automatically migrated, so everyone keeps their current access.

What’s new:

Manage POS users in admin settings
Set up POS users, assign roles, and manage PINs in Settings > Users instead of the POS channel.

Assign organization level roles
Shopify Plus merchants can now grant POS staff access across multiple shops within their organization with a single user profile—no duplicates needed.

Suspend and reactivate seasonal staff
Suspend or deactivate seasonal staff without deleting their accounts. When they return, reactivate them and keep their history.

Assign multiple roles
Create custom roles with the permission sets that make sense for your business. Give staff members as many roles as they need—like Store Manager and Marketer.

New high-trust roles
We’ve created new POS roles to make it easier to identify users with high-trust access. All users have retained their previous permissions, with one exception:

  • POS Administrator (formerly “Full permissions”)
  • POS Device Setup (for setting up new devices)
  • POS User Administrator (for managing users)
  • Organization POS Administrator (for creating, editing and deleting roles across all stores)

Note: The ability to create, edit, or delete roles is now an organization-wide permission, not a shop-level one. For security, we haven’t automatically granted this broader access. If someone on your team previously managed roles for a single shop, you’ll need to assign them the Organization POS Administrator role if you want them to manage roles across all stores.

Assigning existing roles to users is still possible with the POS User Administrator role, which has been assigned to anyone who had that permission previously.

You may need to review and clean up your user and role lists as a result of this change. Learn more in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Unlink a customer from your custom identity provider
item.description:
If your store uses a connected OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider for customer accounts (such as Okta, Auth0, Microsoft Entra ID), you can now unlink a customer from your identity provider directly in the Shopify admin.

When a customer's account is linked to the wrong subject in your identity provider, the customer might see the following error when they try to sign in:

"The sign-in method you used doesn't match this account."

Previously, fixing this required contacting Shopify Support. Now you
can resolve it yourself.

To unlink a customer:
1. From your Shopify admin, go to Customers.
2. Click the customer that you want to unlink.
3. In the customer details section, click Unlink next to your identity provider's ID, such as Okta ID or Auth0 ID.
4. Review the subject ID displayed in the confirmation dialog and compare it with the subject ID for this customer in your identity provider, if you have access to that information. If the subject IDs do not match, unlinking the customer should resolve the The sign-in method you used doesn't match this account. error.
5. Click Unlink to confirm.

After you unlink, the customer is signed out. They can sign back in with their existing credentials, and a new link is created on their next sign-in. The customer's orders, and other store data aren't affected.

This feature is available to stores on the Shopify Plus plan that have connected their own identity provider to customer accounts.

Learn more: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/customers/customer-accounts/sign-in-options/identity-provider/connect#unlink-customer

item.title: Shopify Collective is now available in Australia
item.description:
Shopify Collective is now available to merchants in Australia. Australian
retailers can partner with Australian suppliers to sell their products directly
through their storefronts.

Retailers can expand their catalog without holding inventory or upfront cost.
Suppliers can reach new customers by selling through Australian retailers that
match their brand.

To get started, install Shopify Collective from the Shopify App Store. Both
stores must be based in Australia, use the same currency,
and have Shopify Payments activated.

Learn more in the Shopify Collective help docs

item.title: Shipping performance metrics and Verified Tracking badge in Shopify Collective
item.description:
Suppliers on Shopify Collective can now earn a Verified Tracking badge by maintaining consistent carrier tracking coverage across all of their orders. The badge appears on their supplier profile in Discovery, where badged suppliers increase their discoverability to retailers.

Three shipping metrics now appear on the home page of the Collective: Supplier app: carrier tracking coverage, on-time fulfillment, and on-time delivery.

Metrics are calculated from every order in a supplier's Shopify store, not just Collective orders, so existing shipping work counts toward the badge. Suppliers can see their current coverage, the gap to close, and the steps to get there.

Learn more about this launch in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Multi-location pickup is now available in POS
item.description:
We've just released multi-location pickup in POS, allowing in-store staff to create pickup orders for collection at any of your pickup-enabled locations, right from the cart in POS. The Pickup location row in the cart is now tappable: staff can switch stores in one tap, with live inventory shown for each location so they can pick one that can actually fulfill the order.

Available with POS version 11.8 for POS Pro merchants with two or more pickup-enabled locations in the same country.

Learn more about creating pickup orders at another location in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Improved catalog publishing
item.description:
You can now make edits to your catalog, then save or discard all the changes together.

  • Configure publishing changes across multiple products in a catalog.
  • Review changes, then save or discard them in one action.

Learn more: Create and manage your catalogs

item.title: Schedule, publish, and A/B test new themes and checkout and customer account configurations
item.description:
Rollouts now supports scheduling, gradually publishing and A/B testing your themes and checkout and customer accounts configurations.

You can now:
1. Schedule an entire new checkout or theme to go live at a specific date and time. For example, switch from Dawn to Horizon on a specific date.
2. Temporarily swap to a different theme or checkout setup. For example, activating a BFCM theme for one week with automatic revert.
3. Gradually roll out a new theme or checkout configuration to a percentage of your visitors. For example, rolling out a new branding experience for your customer account pages.
4. Run an A/B test between two entirely different themes or checkout setups to find the winner. For example, A/B testing a new upsell block for your checkout page.
5. Schedule or test localized content per market. For example, test different CTA text for each region to see impact on conversions.

In addition, a copy of your published theme or config is automatically created so you can continue to edit your live theme/checkout independently from your experiment. And with mutually exclusive experiments, you can run multiple live experiments at the same time.

To get started, go to Markets > Rollouts in your Shopify admin and create a Rollout. Learn more about Rollouts in our help documentation.

item.title: Scatter plots and radar charts are now in Shopify Analytics
item.description:
Custom reports in Shopify Analytics now support two new chart types: scatter plots and radar charts. These give you more ways to spot patterns and compare performance across your store data without exporting to a spreadsheet.

Use scatter plots to see how two metrics relate. Plot revenue against units sold per product to find which products move volume but not margin. Plot session count against conversion rate per traffic source to see which channels actually convert, not just bring traffic. Each data point shows up as a dot, so clusters and outliers are easy to spot.

Use radar charts to compare across multiple metrics at once. Look at product categories side by side across average order value, conversion rate, and return rate on one shared axis. The shape that emerges shows the relative strengths and weaknesses of each category at a glance, instead of bouncing between separate line or bar charts.

Both chart types are available now in the visualization picker when you create or edit an existing report with compatible data.

Learn more about chart types in custom reports in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Local payment methods are now available in more countries
item.description:
Offering buyers a familiar, local way to pay can reduce friction and improve conversion at checkout. We've expanded the local payment methods available through Shopify Payments to more countries across Europe and beyond.

Depending on where your business is located, you can now offer:

MobilePay
Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, and Spain.

TWINT
Austria, Belgium, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Spain, and Sweden.

BLIK
Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Norway, Portugal, Slovenia, and Sweden.

Przelewy24
Australia, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Greece, Hong Kong SAR, Hungary, Ireland, Japan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Romania, Singapore, Slovenia, Sweden, and Switzerland.

Eligible buyers will see these payment methods at checkout once you turn them on. To get started, go to Settings > Payments in your Shopify admin and add the local payment methods you'd like to offer.

Learn more about local payment methods

item.title: Clearer payout balance and reserve information in Shopify Payments
item.description:
We’ve updated the Shopify Payments Payouts page to make payout information easier to understand. The amount previously labeled To be paid is now labeled Payout balance, matching the language used across Finance. We’ve also added help text that explains how payout balance is calculated: payments minus refunds, disputes, and fees.

If funds are held in reserve on your account, the Payouts page continues to show the reserved amount separately, with help text explaining that reserved funds are temporarily held to help cover disputes, refunds, and chargeback risk. This update only changes how payout and reserve information is labeled and explained there is no change your payout timing, reserve terms, or payout amount.

Learn more about Shopify Payments payouts and reserves in Shopify Payments in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: A refreshed sign-in page for customer accounts, now customizable in the editor
item.description:
Today, the customer account sign-in page has a refreshed design that gives you greater control over how it looks.

The sign-in page now offers a two-column layout, with the sign-in form shifted to the left and a customizable background image on the right, enabling you to express your brand more visually beyond the logo.

You can now customize and preview the sign-in page directly in the checkout and accounts editor. Set shared settings that apply consistently across all surfaces, and tailor styling elements to give your sign-in page a unique look. Plus merchants have more advanced customization control via the Checkout And Accounts Configuration API.

This is available exclusively on the latest version of customer accounts. If you’re using legacy customer accounts, follow our guide and complete your upgrade.

item.title: View cumulative metrics over time in Analytics
item.description:
We've added cumulative metrics to Analytics so you can see how your metrics build up over time.

When you turn on the Cumulative toggle in the Visualization panel (or add WITH CUMULATIVE_VALUES to your ShopifyQL query), your time-series chart shows a running total instead of individual daily values making it easy to see progress toward a goal or how a metric is trending across a period.

Cumulative view works in three ways:
* On its own: See how a metric accumulates day by day across a date range. Useful for understanding growth patterns at a glance.
* With targets: Compare your running total against a target line to see whether you're on pace to hit your goal.
* With prior-period comparisons: Layer in a comparison to the same period last year (or another period), so you can spot how this period's trajectory compares to the last year.

Learn more here

item.title: Create SMS marketing automations in Shopify Messaging
item.description:
Now you can automatically engage your customers with well-timed SMS messages. Send automated SMS with Shopify Messaging using pre-built templates for abandoned carts, abandoned checkouts, and browse abandonment, or create your own.

Set up your SMS marketing automations from Shopify Messaging > Automations, and manage your SMS spending threshold from Shopify Messaging > Settings.

Learn more about SMS marketing automations in the Shopify Help Center.

item.title: Sell from multiple legal entities in the same country using Shopify Payments
item.description:
Merchants with more complex business structures can now sell from multiple legal entities in the same country using Shopify Payments.

Previously, merchants often needed separate stores or expansion store workarounds when different parts of their business operated under different legal entities in the same country. Now, eligible merchants can configure multiple Shopify Payments accounts within a single store using Markets.

This makes it easier to:
* Sell online and in retail under separate legal entities in the same country
* Support different legal entities for different retail locations
* Separate B2B and D2C sales under different entities
* Attribute sales, payouts, and compliance requirements to the right business entity
* Reduce duplicated admin work across multiple stores
* This update helps merchants keep their business structure flexible while managing more of their operations from one Shopify store.

This update helps merchants keep their business structure flexible while managing more of their operations from one Shopify store.

item.title: Flow: Make test events for your workflows with existing shop data
item.description:
You can now more easily test workflows with existing shop data. Suppose that a recent order was fraudulent and you've built a workflow to block the next one. You can choose that fraudulent order and see if it works. You can also add tests to make sure it doesn't block other other orders.

Additionally, by clicking "Generate test events", Sidekick will analyze the workflow and find real shop data to test the logical paths in your workflow. Each test event contains the data needed to test run your workflow. Review the generated cases, edit or remove any that don't apply, and add your own. You can test it immediately, no further setup required.

For more information, visit the documentation. For questions and feedback, visit the Shopify community.

item.title: The Balance mobile app has a new look
item.description:
The Balance mobile app has been redesigned with a new look and feel. You can still access all the same features and functionality, now with greater ease. You can access your cash, cards, recent activity, and a new flow for transfering money, making it more convenient to manage your finances.

Learn more about the Balance app.

item.title: Updates to Italy's Sardinian province definitions
item.description:
We've updated Italy's province definitions to reflect the Sardinian administrative restoration that took effect in June 2025:
* Gallura Nord-Est Sardegna (OT) is now a selectable province
* Carbonia-Iglesias (CI) has been renamed to Sulcis Iglesiente to match the restored province name.

Merchants shipping to Sardinia may notice updated province names in checkout. Partners using the address validation or autocomplete APIs will get more accurate province assignments for Sardinian addresses.

item.title: Shopify Tax has expanded to Canada
item.description:
Managing Canadian sales tax is complicated, which is why we're committed to making it better. Shopify Tax is bringing brand new features to your admin that will make it easier to collect the right amounts at the right time, and know where your business is liable.

New

Enhanced calculations
Stay confidently compliant selling across Canada knowing that Shopify Tax is accurately calculating sales tax rates (GST, HST, PST, QST, and RST) based on your customer's province and showing each of those rates individually to your buyers.

Smart categorization
Is a single donut a snack, or breakfast? Five donuts? Six? In Canada, six or more donuts is zero-rated as a basic grocery; five or fewer is taxable as a snack food. We may never settle the philosophical question, but at Shopify, we can help you categorize your donuts (and everything else) for tax purposes. Shopify suggests the relevant category for your products and automatically applies the right rate based on Canadian rules.

Furthermore, taxes assessed on shipping will now follow the rate on each individual good, ensuring that zero rated goods or orders with mixed tax rates are accurately taxed.

Tax liability insights per province
Tax liability insights are no longer just at the country level. Now, you’ll be able to track where you may have tax obligations across each province and territory. Liability insights analyzes your store's sales and compares it to government requirements to let you know where and how you may be required to register and collect.

Learn more
